notes: Stated against PMc; restated against PCMc, which keeps the phoneme. Gilbertese once did not tolerate t and k in one morpheme (Marck 1977: 16-17). When they were not in adjacent PMC syllables, the second assimilated to the first: *kiuta > kiika 'octopus', *kinita > kinika 'to pinch s.th.' (p. 332). Otherwise the leftmost was usually deleted (the rows of Bender et al. 2003a).

'The leftmost of these two consonants was deleted when the consonants were in adjacent syllables, unless that would have resulted in a glide-final syllable' (p. 332).
